why: A shell hands a quoted prompt to the program as one argument. Read as plain text, a dashed word of the prompt (a list switch of ls, a recursive-force switch of rm, a type switch of find) matched the one-letter approval group of the CLI in front of it, and honest workflows failed; and a separator inside a quoted URL cut the CLI from the approval switch that follows the URL, so that workflow passed with no note. The pass side is a workflow whose agent steps quote prompts holding those dashed words, and a URL with an ampersand and no switch. The fail side is a workflow whose step quotes a URL with an ampersand and then passes the long approval switch, unquoted, in the same command. Whoever reads quotes as plain text turns both sides wrong: the pass side red and the fail side green. Content is base64 because rebar reads its own caso.json raw.
